config.title: Multiple backgrounds

intro.title: Multiple backgrounds
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a visually rich webpage element by layering multiple background images and colors onto a single container. You will learn the core CSS concept of using the `background` or `background-image` property with comma-separated values to stack backgrounds. The main technologies involved are CSS properties like `background-image`, `background-position`, and `background-size` to control each layer. By the end, you'll be able to create complex, layered visual effects efficiently without extra HTML elements.
intro.usecase: Multiple backgrounds are commonly used in modern web interfaces to create visually rich, layered designs without complex markup. You'll see this technique in hero sections of marketing websites where text overlays a gradient atop an image, in dashboard cards that combine subtle patterns with solid colors for depth, and in interactive UI elements like buttons that show different states through background layering. As a developer, you'll use multiple backgrounds to build sophisticated visual effects efficiently, reducing the need for extra HTML elements while maintaining clean, maintainable code.

objectives: Apply the background property to layer multiple background images on a single element
Configure distinct positioning values for each background layer using background-position
Control the sizing behavior of individual background layers with background-size
Implement background-repeat rules for specific layers to manage tiling patterns
Construct a multi-layered background by combining images with gradient effects
Manipulate the stacking order of background layers to achieve desired visual hierarchy
Integrate multiple background shorthand syntax to streamline CSS declarations

steps.title: Create a CSS file and set up the HTML structure reference
steps.instruction: Create a CSS file and note that we'll be styling a div with class 'multi-bg-container'
steps.hint: You're creating a CSS file that will target an HTML element with the class name 'multi-bg-container'.
steps.seedCode: /* Create CSS rules for the .multi-bg-container class */
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with a comment indicating we'll style the .multi-bg-container element
successCriteria: CSS file contains a comment referencing the .multi-bg-container class
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the CSS file, but make sure to include a comment about styling the .multi-bg-container element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS file should contain a comment about styling the .multi-bg-container element.

steps.title: Set basic container dimensions and background color
steps.instruction: Add width, height, and background-color properties to the .multi-bg-container class to create a visible base container.
steps.hint: Use width and height to define the container's size (e.g., 400px by 300px). Use background-color to set a solid color (e.g., lightblue).
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container class will have defined dimensions and a solid background color, creating a visible rectangular area.
successCriteria: The .multi-bg-container class includes width, height, and background-color properties with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added some properties, but make sure to include all three: width, height, and background-color with appropriate values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The container needs basic styling. Add width, height, and background-color properties to the .multi-bg-container class.

steps.title: Add the first background image using background-image
steps.instruction: Add a background-image property to the .multi-bg-container class with a URL to an image (use a placeholder image URL like 'https://picsum.photos/200').
steps.hint: Use the background-image property with a url() value containing the image URL.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container element will display a single background image.
successCriteria: The .multi-bg-container class has a background-image property with a valid URL.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added the background-image property with a url() value.
steps.feedbackWrong: The background-image property is missing or has incorrect syntax. Try adding: background-image: url('https://picsum.photos/200');

steps.title: Set background-repeat and background-position for the first image
steps.instruction: Add the background-repeat property with the value 'no-repeat' and the background-position property with the value 'center' to the .multi-bg-container rule to control how the first background image repeats and positions itself.
steps.hint: Add these two new properties after the existing background-image property in your CSS rule. Use 'no-repeat' to prevent tiling and 'center' to center the image.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container rule will have background-repeat and background-position properties added to control the first background image's placement.
successCriteria: The .multi-bg-container rule contains both background-repeat: no-repeat; and background-position: center; properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added both background-repeat and background-position properties with the correct values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The CSS rule doesn't yet contain the required background-repeat and background-position properties. Try adding them after the existing background-image property.

steps.title: Add a second background image separated by comma
steps.instruction: Add a second background image URL to the existing background-image property, separated from the first URL by a comma.
steps.hint: You can add multiple background images by listing their URLs in the background-image property, separated by commas. For example: background-image: url('first.jpg'), url('second.jpg');
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container class will have two background images defined in the background-image property, separated by a comma.
successCriteria: The background-image property contains two URLs separated by a comma.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you have exactly two URLs in the background-image property, separated by a comma.
steps.feedbackWrong: The background-image property should contain two URLs separated by a comma. Try adding a second URL after a comma.

steps.title: Set background properties for the second image
steps.instruction: Add background-repeat and background-position values for the second image in the .multi-bg-container class, separated by commas to match the first image's properties.
steps.hint: After the existing background-repeat and background-position values, add a comma followed by the values for the second image. For example: background-repeat: no-repeat, repeat;
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container class will have separate background-repeat and background-position values for each background image, allowing independent control over each layer.
successCriteria: The .multi-bg-container class includes background-repeat and background-position properties with comma-separated values for both images.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both background-repeat and background-position have comma-separated values for both images.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added both background-repeat and background-position properties with comma-separated values matching the two background images.

steps.title: Add a third background layer with a gradient
steps.instruction: Add a linear-gradient() as a third value to the background-image property in your .multi-bg-container rule, separated by commas from the existing image URLs.
steps.hint: Add a third comma-separated value to background-image. Use linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(255,255,255,0.3), rgba(255,255,255,0)) to create a subtle white-to-transparent overlay.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Adding multiple background layers */
background-image: url('image1.jpg'), url('image2.jpg'), linear-gradient(to right, red, blue);
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container will have three background layers: two images and a gradient overlay.
successCriteria: The background-image property contains three comma-separated values, with the third being a linear-gradient() function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a third value to background-image using linear-gradient(), separated by commas from the existing values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gradient layer wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added a third comma-separated value to background-image using linear-gradient().

steps.title: Use the background shorthand property for multiple backgrounds
steps.instruction: Replace all the separate background properties in the .multi-bg-container rule with a single background shorthand property that includes all three layers (two images and one gradient) with their respective repeat and position values.
steps.hint: Combine background-image, background-repeat, and background-position values into one background property, separating each layer's values with commas.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .multi-bg-container rule will use the background shorthand property to apply all three background layers with their specific repeat and position settings in a single line.
successCriteria: The .multi-bg-container rule contains a background shorthand property with three comma-separated layers, each including image/gradient, repeat, and position values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but ensure the background shorthand includes all three layers with their repeat and position values separated by commas.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've replaced the separate background properties with one background shorthand containing three comma-separated layers.

steps.title: Adjust layer order and observe stacking
steps.instruction: In the .multi-bg-container rule, change the order of the three background layers in the background shorthand property so the gradient appears first (on top), followed by the second image,
steps.hint: The background shorthand property currently lists three layers separated by commas. Reorder them so the gradient comes first, then the second image URL, then the first image URL.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example of reordering background layers */
background: linear-gradient(to right, red, blue), url('pattern.png'), url('photo.jpg');
steps.expectedOutcome: The gradient will now appear on top, partially covering the images, demonstrating that background layers stack with the first listed layer on top.
successCriteria: The background shorthand property lists the gradient first, then the second image URL, then the first image URL.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've changed the order in the background shorthand property so the gradient comes first, then the second image, then the first image.
steps.feedbackWrong: The layer order hasn't been changed correctly. Remember to reorder the three layers in the background shorthand property so the gradient is first, followed by the second image, then the first image.

steps.title: the first image
steps.hint: The background shorthand property currently lists three layers separated by commas. Reorder them so the gradient comes first, then the second image URL, then the first image URL.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example of reordering background layers */
background: linear-gradient(to right, red, blue), url('pattern.png'), url('photo.jpg');

steps.feedbackWrong: Check the instruction and try again.
